column1: # GENERATED AND COMMITTED. Signatures below were produced by Python's hmac --
# an oracle outside the JVM and outside PHP -- and cross-checked against
# `openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac`. Both implementations of this protocol are
# checked AGAINST this file; the file is not regenerated from either of them.
# Generating at test time would prove both sides agree with the generator,
# which is one implementation wearing a hat. A committed file is a third party,
# and a change to it shows up as a diff in review.

#   signature  lowercase hex, because PHP's hash_hmac returns lowercase and
#              "whichever case the library happens to produce" is not a contract
# The canonical form is <timestamp> LF <nonce> LF <body>, encoded UTF-8.

# a nonce, so no field boundary can be shifted, and the body is last so it may
# the canonical example, also in docs/protocol.md
# absent body canonicalises as empty, never as the string null
# one byte of body changes the whole signature
# non-ASCII body: UTF-8, not the platform default
# non-ASCII KEY: the key is bytes, and they are UTF-8 too
# the body may contain newlines; it is last, so no boundary moves
